title: Minimum Interval Point Cover
statement:
Choose as few points as possible so every closed interval contains at least one chosen point.

Contract
- `intervals` is non-null. Every interval has `start <= end` and both endpoints are inclusive.
- Return a sorted `int[]` containing a minimum-size set of points that covers all intervals.
- When several minimum covers exist, return the one produced by repeatedly choosing the smallest possible ending point among the remaining intervals.
- Do not mutate the input array or its interval objects.

Examples
- `minimumCoverPoints([1, 3], [2, 5], [6, 7])` returns `[3, 7]`.
- `minimumCoverPoints([1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4])` returns `[2, 4]`.
- `minimumCoverPoints([])` returns `[]`.
hints: Sort intervals by their ending point, not by their starting point.
After choosing an endpoint, it covers every interval whose start is at or before that point.
Skip all covered intervals, then choose the next uncovered interval's end. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: closed intervals as [start,end] pairs, for example: [1,3] [2,5] [6,7]
